AssetLibraryItem.description:
An asset as the library knows it. Carries **both** addresses: the content

BezierPath.description:
A cubic bezier path, structured like Lottie/Bodymovin's "sh" shape so it
round-trips with the web's proven vector-animation format. Segment k→k+1 is
a cubic bezier; tangents are relative to their vertex. All three arrays
must be the same length — the constraint that also makes a path animatable.

BlendMode.description:
Every blend mode the authoring vocabulary contains, supported or not.

The first ten are 1.x's `MATERIAL_BLEND_MODES`, unchanged in name and
order, because a scene authored there must mean the same thing here. 3.20
appends the rest of the Photoshop and After Effects Layer > Blending Mode
menus, so every mode a PSD, an After Effects project or a Figma file names
has exactly one variant and never a nearest neighbour. Together they are
the 27 Photoshop modes and the After Effects ones; the formulas are
EffectCraft's (`crates/color/src/blend.rs` at 9a7d3e7, MIT OR Apache-2.0),
ported with attribution in the render worker.

Two pairs share a formula and stay separate because the source menus name
them separately: `add` (After Effects) and `linear-dodge` (Photoshop's
"Linear Dodge (Add)"); `difference` and `classic-difference` differ only in
how layer opacity applies. `alpha-mask` and `inverse-alpha-mask` are After
Effects' Stencil Alpha and Silhouette Alpha under their 1.x names.

oneOf.description: After Effects Add: `b + s`, over-range kept.

The recorded live fault: 1.x's browser renderer had no `overlay`, so
it drew `screen` instead and nobody was told. It is in the vocabulary
because authors use it; it is not fixed-function, so an engine without
a shader compositing path must refuse it (invariant 18).

After Effects Stencil Alpha: the backdrop is kept where this layer is
opaque, everywhere on the stage.

After Effects Silhouette Alpha: the backdrop is cut out where this
layer is opaque, everywhere on the stage.

Photoshop and After Effects Dissolve: each pixel shows the layer or
the backdrop by a fixed per-pixel threshold against the layer's alpha.
After Effects Dancing Dissolve: Dissolve with a new pattern each frame.

After Effects Classic Color Burn: opacity fades the layer toward white
before the formula applies; negative results are kept.

After Effects Classic Color Dodge: opacity fades the layer toward
black before the formula applies.
Photoshop Linear Dodge (Add): the same formula as `add`.

After Effects Classic Difference: opacity fades the layer toward black
before the formula applies.

After Effects Stencil Luma: the backdrop is scaled by this layer's
luminance, everywhere on the stage.

After Effects Silhouette Luma: the backdrop is scaled by one minus
this layer's luminance, everywhere on the stage.
After Effects Alpha Add: source-over colour, alpha `min(sa + da, 1)`.

After Effects Luminescent Premul: source-over colour without the
layer's own alpha clipping its over-range values.

CubicBezier.description:
Cubic-bezier control points for a custom outgoing easing.

`x1` and `x2` stay in 0–1 because they are time controls; y may overshoot
provided the resulting segment stays within the property's range (opacity
0–1, width/height non-negative). Other properties permit overshoot.
The points are stored with the
key, not solved from neighbouring keys at display time, so a saved scene
means the same curve when it is reopened.

are CSS's, because that is the vocabulary designers hand work over in.

MaterialBinding.description:
What an object's material slot points at.

1.x allowed either a bare material id string *or* an object with
overrides in the same field. An untagged union like that deserialises by
trial, and a shape that nearly matches the wrong arm is accepted silently,
so only the object form is carried.

material kind, so a fill can become a gradient without the material
changing type underneath every object that uses it.

opacity.description: 0–1, multiplied with the object's own opacity.

MaterialKind.description:
What a material fundamentally is.

1.x carried fifteen values here, ten of which its loader rewrote to `pbr`

material.
Physically based, lit by the scene's lights.
Unlit textured — what a lower third's background actually wants.
A custom shader, identified by id.

width.description:
The object's box, in scene units. Every kind has one: a rect and an
image fill it, an ellipse is inscribed in it, paragraph text wraps
inside it, and a binding can drive it — which is why it is on the base
and not repeated per kind.

x.description: Translation in scene coordinates (top-left authoring origin).

zDepth.description: Depth along the view axis; composes additively down the hierarchy.

PhaseKind.description:
The operator phases a scene timeline can name.

These are exactly `crate::mcp::MOTION_PHASES`, and a test below pins them
against it: a phase added to one and not the other fails the gate rather
than producing a scene the agent surface cannot describe.

oneOf.description: Build on. Triggered by Take.
Idle loop after `in` completes. Interruptible at any frame.
Build off. Triggered by Out.
A staged build, triggered by Continue. A timeline may carry several.
How a bound value changes on air without a full re-take.

ProvenanceTool.description: The tool, or for model origin the model, that made or imported the bytes.

RationalRate.description:
A frame rate as an exact rational. Never a float (invariant 12).

29.97 is 30000/1001 and cannot be represented in binary floating point.
Accumulating a rounded rate across an 8-hour soak drifts the clock, so this
type deliberately offers no `f64` constructor.

RectObject.description: A rectangle filling the base box. `radius` is the corner radius.

anchor.description: Object-local pivot in scene pixels; renderers apply T(x,y)·R·S·T(-anchor).

bindings.description:
Bound data paths (object property → data-context path). Opaque here;
the binding contract owns the grammar.

How this layer composites onto what is drawn below it (3.20): the
layer blend mode of Photoshop, After Effects and Figma, from the same
vocabulary materials use (1.3). Omitted from the wire when `normal`,
so a scene that uses no blend mode serialises as it did before.

Primary fill and stroke. Tagged colour values as of 1.4 — a CSS
string carried no source space, and B.1 forbids inferring one.

layerId.description:
The layer this object belongs to (a `Layer` object's id), or empty for
the implicit default layer.

Material slot assignments: slot name → the material bound to it
(1.3). A `BTreeMap` so the wire order is the slot order and two
equal scenes serialise to equal bytes.

Rotation in degrees. `rotation` is the Z axis; X and Y are 3D and
compose down the hierarchy only on meshes (`resolve_hierarchy`).

x.description: Translation in scene coordinates (top-left authoring origin).

zDepth.description: Depth along the view axis; composes additively down the hierarchy.

Revision.description:
Publish revision. Exact-match only: a take against a stale revision is
refused, never coerced (invariant 17).

Rgba.description:
A colour, with the space it was authored in.

Components are 0–1 floats rather than 8-bit bytes because the working
space is linear and 8 bits of linear has visible banding in the shadows.

SceneCanvas.description:
The scene's output canvas. Resolution and rate are configuration, never
constants (ADR-0002 Part C), and the rate is rational (invariant 12).

SceneDocument.description:
The scene document: the unit the Editor authors, the package carries and
the engine prepares. Self-describing — fonts, assets and objects travel
together so a published package never depends on outside state.

activeCameraId.description:
The camera Program renders through. Absent selects the documented
synthetic 2D orthographic camera; a present id must resolve to a
`CameraObject` in this scene.

assets.description: The asset library this scene references.

controls.description:
Operator-facing fields explicitly declared by the template author.
Omitted by pre-11.26 documents, which therefore retain an empty
operator contract when reopened.

dataContext.description: Live data the scene's bindings resolve against.

fonts.description: Fonts available to this scene, resolved package-first.

materials.description:
The materials this scene's objects bind by id. A scene is
self-describing (1.1), so a material slot resolves inside the
document or not at all — a library held anywhere else would make a
published package depend on outside state.

objects.description: The scene graph, in draw order.

revision.description: Monotonic authoring revision; the optimistic-concurrency token (0.8).

textStyles.description:
Named text-style bundles are carried with a scene, while any token
reference they hold resolves against the active project design system.
Older documents omit this list and reopen with no saved styles.

version.description:
Schema version: [`SCENE_SCHEMA_VERSION`] when this build writes it.
The reader upgrades an older version it knows and refuses any other
by name (`SceneSchemaUnsupported`).

workingColorSpace.description:
The space this scene composites in: its project's declared space
(3.15). Required from schema 3; an older document upgrades to
[`WorkingColorSpace::BEFORE_3_15`], the space it was authored in.

SceneEasing.description:
The easing between two keys. Closed and finite: the curve an author chooses
must be one every evaluator knows by name, because a substituted curve is a
visual change no one named (invariant 18).

SceneKeyframe.description: One key on one numeric property channel.

bezier.description: Custom bezier control points, present exactly when easing is custom.

easing.description: Outgoing easing toward the next key.

frame.description: Absolute frame at the scene canvas rate.

value.description: The property's value at that frame, in the property's own units.

SceneObject.description:
The authorable object kinds. A tagged enum, not an open struct: the set of
kinds a scene may contain is a reviewed contract, and the renderer refuses
a kind it does not know by name rather than ignoring it (invariant 18).

SceneTimeline.description:
The scene timeline: its duration and editable per-object channels.

Keys are absolute frames at the canvas rate, unlike preset keys, which are
normalised 0–1 until instantiation (G.6.2). `#[serde(default)]` keeps a
scene authored before the field existed valid and equivalent to an empty
channel set.

channels.description: Editable keyframe channels, one per object/property.

durationFrames.description: Total duration in frames at the canvas rate.

phases.description:
Named operator phases over those channels (11.25). `#[serde(default)]`
keeps a scene authored before phases existed valid and unphased.

ShapeObject.description:
An After-Effects-style shape layer: a bezier path with fill and stroke
(the base carries both) and AE's Trim Paths.

anchor.description: Object-local pivot in scene pixels; renderers apply T(x,y)·R·S·T(-anchor).

bindings.description:
Bound data paths (object property → data-context path). Opaque here;
the binding contract owns the grammar.

layer blend mode of Photoshop, After Effects and Figma, from the same
vocabulary materials use (1.3). Omitted from the wire when `normal`,
so a scene that uses no blend mode serialises as it did before.

compoundPaths.description: Additional subpaths for compound paths; `path` remains primary.

fill.description:
Primary fill and stroke. Tagged colour values as of 1.4 — a CSS
string carried no source space, and B.1 forbids inferring one.

The layer this object belongs to (a `Layer` object's id), or empty for
the implicit default layer.

(1.3). A `BTreeMap` so the wire order is the slot order and two
equal scenes serialise to equal bytes.

rotation.description:
Rotation in degrees. `rotation` is the Z axis; X and Y are 3D and
compose down the hierarchy only on meshes (`resolve_hierarchy`).

trimStart.description:
AE Trim Paths, as percentages of the path's total length: the stroke
draws from `trim_start` to `trim_end`, rotated by `trim_offset`.
Absent — or 0/100/0 — draws the whole stroke. The window is
stroke-only; the fill always covers the whole region, which is what
separates a wipe reveal from a scaling mask.

Precisely (3.13): start and end lie in 0–100 and a start after the end
draws the same window as end to start; the offset is any finite
percentage, 100 being one full turn (After Effects' 360°), and a window
that passes the end of the path wraps to its beginning. Length is
measured in the shape's own coordinates, so a non-uniform scale does
not move the window, and each subpath of a compound shape is trimmed
with the same window (After Effects' "simultaneously"). A value outside
its domain refuses `ShapeTrimInvalid`.

image fill it, an ellipse is inscribed in it, paragraph text wraps
inside it, and a binding can drive it — which is why it is on the base
and not repeated per kind.

x.description: Translation in scene coordinates (top-left authoring origin).

zDepth.description: Depth along the view axis; composes additively down the hierarchy.

SlabBevel.description: One bevel of a slab, measured inward from its outline.

depth.description: Z depth the bevel occupies, in scene units.

size.description: Width of the bevel, inward from the slab outline, in scene units.

SlabProperties.description:
XPression-style slab controls: a rounded, skewed extrusion with
independent front and back bevels. Geometry only — face culling is a
material property and arrives with 1.3's material model.

cornerRadius.description: Corner radius of the slab outline, in scene units.

culling.description: Object-level face culling, matching XPression's slab control (1.3).

skew.description: Horizontal displacement between the slab's bottom and top edges.

skewTexture.description: Whether texture coordinates follow the skewed outline.

SourceColorSpace.description:
What a colour or a texture was authored in. There is no `Unknown`: an
untagged source is a defect the importer must refuse, not a value a
renderer may guess at (B.1, "never infer").

oneOf.description:
IEC 61966-2-1. What a hex literal, a PNG without an ICC profile and
most authoring tools mean.
Already linear — no decode on the way in.
ITU-R BT.709 with its own transfer curve. Broadcast source material.

StyleColor.description:
A text-style colour, either literal or resolved from the active project
design system when the style is applied.

StyleNumber.description:
A numeric text-style value, either literal or resolved from the active
project design system when the style is applied.

TextAutoFit.description: What to do when shaped text does not fit its box. Never silently clipped.

TextCase.description:
Case applied when the text is drawn, not when it is typed: the authored
characters stay as they are, so a data binding can replace the text and
the case still applies, and switching it off returns the author's own
capitalisation.

TextDecoration.description:
Underline and strikethrough: drawn from the font's metrics rather than
shaped, so they are object state and not part of the font definition.

TextDirection.description:
Base direction. `Auto` resolves from the first strong character, which is
what makes bidi text (3.6) correct without the author declaring it.

TextLayout.description: Point text grows from its origin; paragraph text wraps inside the base box.

TextObject.description:
A text object. The font is referenced by id into the scene's font list —
never by a system family name (ADR-0002 A.4's one rule), which is why
family, weight, style and stretch are on `FontDefinition` and not here.
The colour is the base's `fill`.

Bound data paths (object property → data-context path). Opaque here;

The layer this object belongs to (a `Layer` object's id), or empty for
the implicit default layer.

letterSpacing.description: Tracking, in thousandths of an em — After Effects' unit.

lineHeight.description:
Line height as a multiple of `size`. Absent means the font's own
metrics, which is not the same as 1.0.

(1.3). A `BTreeMap` so the wire order is the slot order and two

image fill it, an ellipse is inscribed in it, paragraph text wraps

zDepth.description: Depth along the view axis; composes additively down the hierarchy.

TextStyle.description:
A named, reusable subset of a text object's appearance.

Optional entries are deliberately absent rather than defaults: applying a
style must not overwrite a property its author did not declare.

TimelinePhase.description: One named span of the scene timeline.

endFrame.description: One past the last frame. See the module note on why this is exclusive.

name.description:
Distinguishes several `continue` phases from each other. Absent means
the kind names it uniquely, which is true of every kind but `continue`.

startFrame.description: First frame of the phase, inclusive.

TokenRef.description:
A token reference in a preset: `{duration.base}`, `{easing.brand-in}`.

A preset that hardcodes a value instead of referencing a token is a bug for
the same reason a component hardcoding a hex colour is (G.6.1). Kept as a
string with a checked shape rather than a free string, so a malformed
reference is caught at parse, not at render.

WorkingColorSpace.description:
The space a project composites in (build plan 3.15; ADR-0002 B.1 as
amended 12 October 2026). Blending, alpha compositing, gradient
interpolation, filtering and effects all happen in it; tagged sources are
converted in once and an [`OutputTransform`] converts out once.

There is no `Default`. A project declares its space and every scene in it
carries the same one, because a guessed space changes every
semi-transparent pixel without anyone having chosen it (invariant 18).

oneOf.description:
Display-referred sRGB: components stay sRGB-encoded while they
composite. Figma, Photoshop and After Effects composite this way by
default, so an imported design reproduces. A new project's space.

Linear-light sRGB primaries: physically linear compositing. The space
every scene composited in before 3.15.

WritingMode.description: CSS `writing-mode` values, which is what the shaper (3.6) consumes.
